page.overview:
What is The Fellowship of the Ring (film)?

The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is a 2001 fantasy adventure film, directed by Peter Jackson. It is the first of the , adapting the of the by J.R.R. Tolkien. The film tells the story of young hobbit Frodo Baggins who, accompanied by eight companions, embarks on a journey to destroy the One Ring in the fires of Mount Doom.

The screenplay was first started by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, and Peter Jackson in 1997, and eventually it was reaching completion in tandem with its filming, on location in New Zealand. The film had a budget of about $180 million U.S. dollars, principal photography took 14 months, and post production continued long after that. It was also a great box office success, making over $868 million worldwide on its initial release and was the fifth highest-grossing film of all time at the time of its release (behind Titanic, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace, and Jurassic Park). After the 2011 re-release of The Lion King and the 2012 re-release of Finding Nemo, it was the 68th highest-grossing film of all time.

The film was the first live-action film adaptation of Middle-earth to be released.

Sauron, the Dark Lord who has been defeated years ago during the War of the Last Alliance by Elendil, Isildur, and Elrond, has awakened and threatens to conquer Middle-earth. To stop this ancient evil once and for all, Frodo Baggins must destroy the One Ring in the fires of Mount Doom. Men (Aragorn and Boromir), Hobbits (Sam, Merry, and Pippin), a wizard (Gandalf), an Elf (Legolas), and a Dwarf (Gimli) form a fellowship to help him on his quest.
